clue.text: An American writer describes brief WI music disaster

parts.note: an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the writer's name goes around the music

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales of horror

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the music loses its final letter

parts.note: calypso is the folk music of the West Indies (WI)

explanation.surface: A US author writes about a West Indian music festival that went badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means drawing round, so the writer's name wraps the shortened music.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a cataclysmic event on a world-ending scale, the ultimate catastrophe.

clue.text: Quietly back complaint in plant

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: Someone quietly suffering a bad back while working among the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago, also called leadwort, is a flowering shrub with blue or white blooms.

clue.text: Fodder is tossed, then left to mature

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the two letters of is are mixed up

parts.note: to age is to mature or ripen with time

explanation.surface: Animal feed is turned over and then left to ripen, as on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Silage is grass or other green crops fermented and stored as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Finish off incredible eastern story

indicators.note: to finish off something is to take off its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a tall story is an incredible one

explanation.surface: Telling someone to wrap up an unbelievable story from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' removes the last L of TALL, leaving TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative or account, the same as a story.

clue.text: Order people filling in survey to start again

indicators.note: filling in means going inside, so these pieces sit within the survey word

parts.note: a recce is a reconnaissance, a survey of ground
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
men are people

explanation.surface: An instruction for staff filling in a questionnaire to go back to the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To recommence is to begin again after a pause, synonymous with restarting.

clue.text: Hybrid bulbel the Spanish introduced

indicators.note: introduced means brought in, so the article is placed among the letters
a hybrid is a cross, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A cross-bred plant arising from the Spanish variety being brought into Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: BULBEL with EL put in is rearranged. As a whole the clue describes the plant: the Spanish species, introduced to Britain, hybridises with the native one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish species of this blue spring woodland flower crosses with the native kind, producing hybrids.

clue.text: Suffolk river or its source?

parts.note: a well or spring is where a river rises, its source

explanation.surface: A query whether this is the Suffolk river or where it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The river also gave the writer Eric Blair his pen name, the theme of this puzzle; Suffolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orwell is the river flowing through Ipswich in Suffolk to the North Sea.

clue.text: A bit like Snowball, short of energy with running

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the energy letter is taken away

parts.note: Snowball is the white pig in Animal Farm; a snowball is also white
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Describing something partly snowball-like, lacking energy as it rolls along.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: 'with running' adds a second wordplay, an anagram of WITH, which also gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in not a whit, a tiny bit.

clue.text: Pound nut holding a large stone

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the head word goes around the rest

parts.note: nut is slang for the head, as is pate
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing
a pit is the stone of a fruit

explanation.surface: Smash a nut that has a large stone inside, as if cracking it open.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart pounds when it palpitates, beating rapidly and forcefully.

clue.text: Popular chestnut fencing timber

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the words surround the answer

explanation.surface: Chestnut is a popular wood for making fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Larch is a conifer whose durable wood is used in building and fencing.

clue.text: Fellow member retired during programme

indicators.note: during means within, so the reversed limb sits inside the programme

parts.note: code is a computer program

indicators.note: retired means withdrew, so the limb word is read backwards

parts.note: an arm is a member, a limb

explanation.surface: A fellow belonging to a pension scheme who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' reads as a club member but is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade is a companion or fellow member, especially in a party or the forces.

clue.text: Old container brought round before getting pig out

indicators.note: brought round means placed around, so the container goes about the next piece

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquid
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An old trough is fetched before a pig is let out to feed.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is slang for gorging, eating far too much.

clue.text: Let's stand back to front

definitions.note: read as Let + 's (is): the definition is Let, to rent out

indicators.note: the back letter is brought to the front of the word

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A suggestion that everyone stand facing the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's' is read as 'Let is'. 'back to front' moves the final L of EASEL to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To let property is to rent it out under a contract, the same as to lease it.

clue.text: Obliged school to enrol representative English learners

indicators.note: to enrol is to take in, so the school word holds the others

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
L is learner, as on a learner driver's plate; two give LL

explanation.surface: A school was made to admit an MP and English students.
explanation.definitionFit: Being compelled is being forced or required to do something, i.e. obliged.

clue.text: Officer carried over short distance with soldier

parts.note: c/o is the bookkeeping abbreviation for carried over
mm, millimetre, is a short distance
and means with, in addition
a soldier ant is a worker of a colony

explanation.surface: An officer was carried a short way along with a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A commandant is the officer in charge of a military establishment or force.

clue.text: Heated dry nuts, finally parched, desiccated

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
finally points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Nuts roasted dry until they end up parched and shrivelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food being heated; it is the anagram signal for HEATED DRY, followed by D from 'finally parched'.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiccated food has had all its moisture removed, like dried fruit or coconut.

clue.text: Munch nosh all up, out eating good pub fare

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the scrambled letters hold the next piece
out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eat up all your food, out somewhere enjoying a good meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MUNCH NOSH ALL UP around G from 'good'. A ploughman's lunch is a British pub dish of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This cold plate of bread, cheese and pickle is a classic menu item served in British pubs.

clue.text: Statesman, say, circulated paper I submitted

definitions.note: a citizen of a state, here one from the state of Georgia

indicators.note: circulated means turned round, so the example abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

indicators.note: submitted means put in, so I goes inside the paper

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal speaking for a group

explanation.surface: A political figure, for instance, handing round a newspaper he wrote for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' is read as an inhabitant of a state. 'circulated' turns EG into GE; 'submitted' puts I into ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the US state of Georgia, or the country, is a citizen of that state.

clue.text: Emperor shows his dissent, seizing a stick

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the refusal surrounds the rest

parts.note: the emperor is French, and his word of dissent is non
a pole is a long stick

explanation.surface: An emperor shows his disagreement by grabbing a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers to the French emperor, so the no is French NON. Napoleon is also the tyrant pig in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: European Union abandoning work worried complex

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the letter for union is dropped

parts.note: labour is work
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A worried European Union ditching a complicated work programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' gives E, not 'European Union' as EU. 'abandoning' removes U from LABOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate and detailed, with many parts, i.e. complex.

clue.text: Fan mail distributed by branch for 7's 23 across

definitions.note: a short novel by the author named at another clue

indicators.note: distributed means dispersed, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: an arm is a branch, of a tree or organisation

explanation.surface: Letters from admirers handed out by a local office.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition cross-refers: 7 down's writer, and 23 across's short work.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's 1945 satire of the Russian Revolution is a short novel about farmyard animals.

clue.text: Tasteful priest delivered clothing

indicators.note: clothing means covering, so the spoken word wraps round the priest

parts.note: to deliver a speech is to say it, so said

explanation.surface: A priest with good taste handed over some clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tasteful' here means having flavour, not stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid means having a strong pleasant flavour, so full of taste.

clue.text: Contest opens very tense council

indicators.note: opens here means splits open, so the contest word goes into the others

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: A contest begins at a very tense council meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was an elected workers' council in revolutionary Russia.

clue.text: Call in agent, getting ruffled?

indicators.note: in places the phone call inside the agent word

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A worried person rings an agent, getting flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruffled' suggests flustered, but a ruff is a frilled collar, so ruffled means having a frilled border.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fringed has a decorative edging, like a ruffle on a garment.

clue.text: See 20
Short work made of some material star collected

indicators.note: collected means gathered in, so the star contains the cloth measure

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens
an ell is an old length for measuring cloth

explanation.surface: A short book made from a quantity of cloth a star gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction shorter than a novel but longer than a short story.

clue.text: Handle staff rises by end of June

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means read upwards, so the staff word reverses

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A staff handle goes up by late June.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name or title, as in a CB radio handle.

clue.text: Rope in Spanish mare at Ascot boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A Spanish horse at Ascot racecourse being put in its stall.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse. 'Spanish' hints the rope is a Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reata is a lasso or lariat, a rope used for catching cattle in the American West.

clue.text: Wee hit

definitions.meaning: a hit record at the top of the charts

explanation.surface: A small hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call urinating this; also the bestselling chart record.
